newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-PUSHPAKUMARA PEGS BACK WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PUSHPAKUMARA PEGS BACK WEST INDIES.

text.p: Sri Lankan paceman Ravindra Pushpakumara struck twice in successive overs to restrict West Indies to 135 for four at lunch on the second day of the first test on Saturday.
Pushpakumara reached the interval with figures of three for 42, including the vital wicket of Brian Lara who fell cheaply when umpire Lloyd Barker upheld a confident caught behind appeal.
Lara uncharacteristically waited for the umpire's decision and television replays raised doubt as to whether there had been an edge.
Pushpakumara had also sent back debutant Floyd Reifer for a well-made 29, ruffling the home side who had looked comfortably placed at 94 for one in reply to Sri Lanka's 223 all out.

Sherwin Campbell completed his eighth test half-century off 115 balls with three fours, only to smash a savage square-cut to gully where Muthiah Muralitharan held a brilliant catch to leave West Indies on 122 for four.
